strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#64330 / PR#66183 by building pandas at the buggy commit da4c75bc72f9 with a Cython toolchain, installing pyarrow so the non-null-NaN test is not skipped, and running the three new tests in pandas/tests/groupby/methods/test_quantile.py. The non-null-NaN tests (pyarrow and masked FloatingArray) are the ones expected to transition on any platform; the all-NaT test only transitions on arm64 (where NaN to i8 gives 0 instead of iNaT), so it must be run on arm64 hardware to show a buggy failure.

system_packages: a C compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
pinned_because: No version pins: NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython have documented_constraint null and era_ceiling null, so their versions are unbounded. I chose current releases compatible with the buggy checkout's build backend and say so here rather than relying on documentation.

pyarrow is unpinned and added only because the non-null-NaN test calls pytest.importorskip('pyarrow'); without it the test is silently skipped rather than failing, which would give a false no-transition result.
meson-python, meson and ninja are assumed from the standard pandas build backend; they are not stated in the evidence and should be checked against the buggy revision's pyproject.toml.

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision da4c75bc72f9, test_groupby_quantile_nonnull_nan_pyarrow and test_groupby_quantile_nonnull_nan_masked must FAIL because the non-null NaN is copied into the quickselect buffer and the grouped quantiles differ from the non-grouped Series.quantile values (non-monotonic). test_groupby_quantile_all_nat_group must FAIL on arm64 (NaN cast to i8 yields 1970-01-01 instead of NaT) and may PASS on x86-64 because NaN cast to i8 there equals INT64_MIN, which is NaT. On the fixed revision all three must PASS on both platforms.
strategy.numerical_probe: Run the pyarrow case in isolation on the buggy build and print result.to_numpy() against pd.Series(arr).quantile(qs).to_numpy() to confirm the non-monotonic values before relying on the assertion.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: 1970-01-01 (Unix epoch, i.e. 0 as i8) on arm64

risks: The all-NaT defect is platform dependent: on x86-64 Linux or macOS the buggy build returns INT64_MIN, which equals NaT, so test_groupby_quantile_all_nat_group will not transition there. A real buggy failure needs arm64 (Apple Silicon or Graviton).

The non-null NaN defect is not guaranteed to fail for every buffer layout; the tests depend on the NaN landing in the quickselect path, so a buggy pass is possible if the data ordering does not disturb the selected quantiles.
If pyarrow is missing, test_groupby_quantile_nonnull_nan_pyarrow is skipped by importorskip, which reads as a pass and would hide a non-transition.
The FloatingArray test constructs a non-null NaN directly, so it depends on pandas masked-array handling of NaN with mask False; behaviour across pandas versions is not documented in the evidence.
Signed zero and subnormal values are not covered by any passage and are not exercised by these tests.
The tolerance used by tm.assert_series_equal and tm.assert_numpy_array_equal is not quantified in the evidence; the tests rely on library defaults.
The build requires a C compiler and Cython to regenerate groupby.pyx; a stale build artifact will mask the fix, so force a rebuild after checking out each revision.
Build-backend versions are unbounded per the era table and were not verified against the buggy commit's pyproject.toml.

oracle.tolerance: tm.assert_series_equal and tm.assert_numpy_array_equal defaults (not quantified in evidence)
oracle.reference_source: non-grouped pandas Series.quantile on the same data, and the explicit expected Series in the test
oracle.why: The expected values are small exact floats (1.0 to 5.0) and a NaT, so exact equality is expected in practice; the default tolerance is only a fallback.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The pyarrow and masked tests see grouped quantile values that differ from the non-grouped or explicit expected values because the non-null NaN corrupts kth_smallest ordering, so the assert fails. The all-NaT test sees 1970-01-01 instead of NaT only on arm64; on x86 it sees NaT and passes.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: All three tests pass on the fixed revision on both x86-64 and arm64, since the NaN is skipped in both the count and copy passes and all-NaT positions are mapped explicitly to iNaT.
